description:
The AID WHEN OTHER arm - app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:98-102 - reached by a key that resolves to nothing at all. EVALUATE EIBAID at :90-103 has four arms and this is the last of them: DFHENTER at :91-92, DFHPF3 at :93-95, DFHPF4 at :96-97, then WHEN OTHER. DFHPA3 is x'6B' and it is the interesting way in: app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy tests twenty-eight AIDs - DFHENTER, DFHCLEAR, DFHPA1, DFHPA2 and DFHPF1 through DFHPF24, with PF13 to PF24 folded back onto PFK01 to PFK12 - and DFHPA3 is not among them even though DFHPA1 and DFHPA2 immediately before it are, so common.PfKeyResolver returns no key whatsoever for it. That copybook EVALUATE has no WHEN OTHER of its own and does not pre-clear CCARD-AID, which is exactly why no key at all is a distinct answer from some key this program does not name - case18 takes the second route with DFHPF12, which the resolver does map, to PFK12. A resolver rewritten to hand back a default key would pass one of the two and fail the other. EIBAID is tested inline here, COUSR01C being one of the twelve programs that do not COPY CSSTRPFY, so the single shared resolver has to reproduce those inline tests as identical boolean outcomes.

The arm does three things rather than two, and in source order: :99 raises WS-ERR-FLG, :100 moves -1 into FNAMEL of COUSR1AI, and :101 moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into WS-MESSAGE, before :102 performs SEND-USRADD-SCREEN. The message derivation is written out because two of its three steps change the width. app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy declares CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY as PIC X(50) over a literal of forty-nine characters - forty of text and nine spaces - and the PICTURE supplies the fiftieth, which is what common.SystemMessages reproduces; the MOVE at :101 pads that into WS-MESSAGE PIC X(80) as forty plus forty; and MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :188 narrows it into ERRMSGO PIC X(78) of app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY:164 as forty plus thirty-eight, truncating on the right. Both channels are pinned because the two widths are two different observations: a translation that skipped the narrowing, or that truncated on the left, would satisfy only one of them.

Four properties of the legacy design are asserted here rather than corrected. The transaction returns normally - expectedReturnCode is 0, because COUSR01C never moves to RETURN-CODE and carries no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere, so even a rejected key is reported on the screen and nowhere else. No attribute is written on this path, so ERRMSGC stays the map default DFHDFCOL: MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :254 belongs to the successful write and to nothing else. There is no asterisk marker and no per-field DFHRED either, because :57 carries COPY DFHATTR commented out and this program copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY - zero occurrences of both, verified. And USRSEC is untouched: expectedWrites is empty while expectedFinalState brings the ten seeded rows back byte-identical with no eleventh row, which is the positive form of the assertion that a key this program does not name writes nothing. The cursor lands on First Name regardless, which the key press had nothing to do with.

Seeding and determinism. There is no usrsec fixture in app/data/ASCII - the nine that exist describe other datasets - so the ten rows are the in-stream data of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 stated at the fifty-seven characters the JCL carries, while STEP02 at :63-73 defines the cluster with KEYS(8,0) and RECORDSIZE(80,80). The twenty-three bytes of SEC-USR-FILLER that app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares are supplied once, at seed time, by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never at comparison time, so a width disagreement in a failure is always a real difference. SEC-USR-PWD stays plaintext at eight characters because that is what the program writes and what COSGN00C compares; hashing it would change behaviour. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the instant all twenty cases of this folder share, which is what makes CURDATEO 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO 23:12:34 assertable at all, and the code page is named explicitly as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default.

Where the other WHEN OTHER lives, and why it is not in this slot. The build plan for case17 described the second one - the arm of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :267-273, taken after the EXEC CICS WRITE at :240-248 fails - driven by a residual outcome no sibling uses. In this suite that arm is already pinned twice, by two genuinely different residual outcomes: case10 forces NOT_FOUND, CICS RESP 13, and case13 forces the generic FileStatus.Outcome.OTHER, the permanent-error shape that reports no RESP at all. Both produce the same twenty-one character Unable to Add User... text padded to eighty and then to seventy-eight, and the same FNAMEL cursor, which is what proves that arm a genuine catch-all rather than a two-value list. G47 is therefore already complete for the single add call site - '00' by case01, case11, case12 and case20, '22' by case08 as DUPKEY and case09 as DUPREC against the real seeded ADMIN001 key, '23' by case10, and any other value by case13 - and COUSR01CParityTest.everyAidArmIsDriven binds case17 to DFHPA3, so restating the write arm here would have cost the only route that proves the resolver returns nothing rather than a default key. Two properties of that arm are recorded here rather than left unstated: its :268 DISPLAY of RESP and REAS is commented out in the source, so not even the response codes reach an operator and the generic text is all anyone sees - a diagnosability weakness this migration preserves rather than fixes, and one it must not restore as a log statement - and its cursor is FNAMEL where the duplicate arm at :265 uses USERIDL.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived, by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl:78-110, :184-196 and :214-233, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the six-span eighty-byte record, app/cpy-bms/COUSR01.CPY for the twelve field widths and for ERRMSGO PIC X(78), app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy for the message literal, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the two forty-character titles with the Credit Card Demo Application (CCDA) alternative commented out, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the sixteen commarea fields, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99 for FILE(USRSEC) with STATUS(ENABLED), OPENTIME(FIRSTREF), RECOVERY(NONE) and ADD(YES), and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl for the seed data. None of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, which section 0.7.6 of the Agent Action Plan proves impossible in this environment with eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, an indexed file handler reported disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository. Twenty cases, field-for-field diffing and a required diff count of zero all stand; only the provenance of the expected values is substituted.
